name: tabor-holy-grail
title: The holy Grail
description: Trace the vessel through Arthurian literature and later Christian associations.
sections: Chrétien de Troyes presents a grail in Perceval. Robert de Boron’s later verse romance ties the vessel to the Last Supper and Joseph of Arimathea.
Matthew 26:27–29 describes the cup at the supper. The literary history of the Grail records how later writers gave the vessel its own story.

In the Grail Castle episode, a young woman carries the graal in both hands. Perceval leaves the question of whom it serves unasked. This transcription draws on the Old French manuscript BnF français 794.
Wolfram von Eschenbach’s Parzival presents the Grail as a stone with life-sustaining powers. This version belongs to a different branch of the medieval Grail tradition.

Valencia Cathedral’s chapter statutes record the Santo Cáliz in the cathedral’s custody from March 18, 1437. Its identification with the Last Supper belongs to liturgical tradition. First-century custody remains unverified.
A future entry can document each candidate with its earliest recorded attribution and a chain of custody.
